title: Tests with a fixed time limit fail on a loaded machine
what: 12 cores; 20 test files hold a timeout of 10 s or more (grep, 28 Oct). Find the cause, not one example (principle 6): list every test that runs a subprocess or a step with a fixed wall-clock limit; for each, make the test independent of machine speed (an injected clock or budget, or a limit derived from the work) or move it where load cannot reach it. Measure what drives load to 27 (gate slots x test jobs x lanes' own test runs) and whether the gate's job count or slot count should depend on the machine's free capacity.
why: 28 Oct, the second time in one day: tests/test_rules_gate_isolation.py:22 hit its 200 s subprocess timeout in the stub-guard branch's gate (4 test jobs, 1277 s, load average 27), and passed alone in 55 s; earlier tests/test_precheck.py's 3 s budget failed the same way (fixed separately). Neither test was in the changes they turned red. Each red gate of this kind costs a gate fixer and a gate rerun (about 20-25 min) and stops a lane.
failing_case: Run the full gate while another gate and 4 agents run their tests: tests/test_rules_gate_isolation.py fails at its 200 s timeout though it passes alone in 55 s.
pass_cases: The same load: the gate is green 20 times in a row on those tests.
A test that really hangs still fails, by a limit tied to the work, not to the clock of a busy machine.

fact: 29 Oct, gate of wt/refuse-folder-and-pattern-entries-in-whe at a91e4a4a: tests/test_rules_gate_isolation.py:22 test_rules_tests_command_passes_in_the_order_unittest_runs_them hit its own 200 s subprocess timeout while the gate's library tests took 2109 s in all; run alone it passes in 51 s (2 tests). Same day the precheck's changed-tests step hit its 230 s cap at load ~35 on 12 cores on wt/queue-time-estimates-are-guesses-with-no. Both red steps found nothing wrong in the change.

29 Oct ~01:00 UTC, relay land of wt/guard-main-refuses-a-script-that-only-na, gate of f2f761db: library tests took 3521 s (about 240 s on a quiet machine, measured the same day on wt/type-check-subfolders-and-cap-module-siz) and failed only on two timing tests: test_rules_gate_isolation test_rules_tests_command_passes_in_the_order_unittest_runs_them (200 s subprocess timeout) and test_numbers test_session_end_hook_is_fast_on_a_large_ledger (0.61 s against a 0.3 s limit). Load averages after it: 11.5 / 23.5 / 29.8 on 12 cores, with 5 lanes gating. Second red gate from timing in one night that found nothing wrong in the change.

29 Oct measured cause of tonight's timing failures (test_rules_gate_isolation 200 s cap, test_numbers SessionEnd 0.3 s cap, precheck changed-tests 230 s cap): 59 leaked fixture gate scripts from tests/test_land.py::test_land_lock_frees_on_kill, 312 new processes a second, CPU 93.5% system. The limits still fail on any loaded machine, so this item stands; the leak is its own item.

29 Oct ~08:00, gate of wt/refuse-folder-and-pattern-entries-in-whe at 35ecd293: tests/test_gate_stops.py:77 test_f2_an_interrupted_runner_leaves_no_gate_command failed in the inert step's nested run (829 s) with 'the gate command is still running after its runner was interrupted', while the same tests passed in the outer run (1108 s); the change touches no gate code. Its wait is the until() helper's fixed window, so it belongs to the same class: a fixed wall-clock wait that a loaded machine overruns.

29 Oct ~09:00, gate rerun of wt/refuse-folder-and-pattern-entries-in-whe: tests/test_gate_slots.py test_a_gate_killed_with_sigkill_frees_its_slot failed with condition not reached within 30 s, at load 30-35 on 12 cores (6 lanes building, 13 leaked fixture scripts alive). Third red gate of this branch from a fixed wait, none from the change.

29 Oct 09:55, measured on wt/tests-with-a-fixed-time-limit-fail-on-a: 12 cores; load average 8.6 at 09:44 rose to 32.7 at 09:48 while one precheck (changed tests, parallel jobs) and a pytest run of 5 gate test files ran beside other lanes' gates (ps showed 5 relay gate processes of other lanes and 8 test worker processes). The precheck changed-tests step then hit its 230 s cap, the same class. The 16 changed test files alone pass in 199 s at load 8. Driver: gate slots x RELAY_TEST_JOBS x lanes' own precheck runs add up with no look at free capacity. Not decided: whether jobs or slots should follow free capacity (needs the owner's number). Every remaining fixed 20-120 s test wait is raised to the 600 s hang bound in this change.
